Title: HIO-EMERGING ISSUE: WA-WebSites:FUNCTIONS Parent issue for storage‑access failures log (“Unable to get table reference or create table…”) in App Insights every 10‑min
Content:
# Emerging Issue Analysis

*Generated on: 2025-05-16 23:45:03 UTC*

## Condition

Azure Functions Apps log the error 'Unable to get table reference or create table. Aborting write operation.' in Application Insights every 10 minutes. The error details include Azure.RequestFailedException with Status: 403 (Forbidden) and ErrorCode: AuthorizationFailure or AuthorizationPermissionMismatch. This occurs when the Functions runtime cannot access the Table Storage for diagnostic events, typically due to missing 'Storage Table Data Contributor' role for the managed identity or network restrictions on the storage endpoint. The error does not impact app health or availability.

## Estimated Time for Action/Resolution

The hotfix rollout for affected versions (4.1039.500, 4.839.500, 4.639.500) is expected to complete by approximately 2025-05-23. No ETA for 4.40 family release yet.

## Internal Mitigation Steps

A code fix is being rolled out: the Functions Runtime will disable the Diagnostic Events service if it cannot write to Table Storage, preventing further error logs. Hotfixes are being applied to 4.39 (4.1039.500, 4.839.500, 4.639.500) and will be included in the 4.40 family. Update documentation to clarify required permissions for identity-based connections. Monitor rollout and communicate status to support teams.

## Customer Mitigation Steps

Customers can: 1) Grant the 'Storage Table Data Contributor' role to the identity used by the Function App for the Storage Account; 2) Add a log filter in host.json to suppress these logs: {"version": "2.0", "logging": {"logLevel": {"Microsoft.Azure.WebJobs.Script.WebHost.Diagnostics.DiagnosticEventTableStorageRepository": "None"}}}; 3) Disable Diagnostic Event Logging via app setting: AzureWebJobsFeatureFlags=DisableDiagnosticEventLogging; 4) Fix network/firewall issues preventing access to Table Storage. These errors do not impact app health.

## Root Cause Analysis

The issue is caused by the Functions Runtime attempting to write diagnostic events to Table Storage every 10 minutes. If the managed identity lacks the 'Storage Table Data Contributor' role or if the Table endpoint is unreachable (due to network/firewall/private endpoint misconfiguration), the operation fails with a 403 error. The error is logged in Application Insights but does not affect app health. The problem became more visible after support for identity-based connections was added in version 4.37, and documentation did not specify the required permissions. The fix disables the diagnostic events feature if storage access fails, preventing repeated error logs.
